always.title: Fake News Detector
always.lede: Paste a news article. Two text models score whether its writing style resembles the fake or the real articles they were trained on.
always.scope: Trained on about 1,600 labelled news articles. It scores writing style; it does not check facts.
always.label: Article text
always.placeholder: Paste the full article, not just the headline.
always.samples_intro: Try a text written for this demo:

headlines.unrecognised: Too few words the models know

error.internal_error: Something went wrong on the server

bodies.first_load: Paste an article or load a sample. Scores appear here.
bodies.no_signal_both: Both models scored this within 3 points of an empty text (59 % fake · 41 % real), so the score says nothing about these words.
bodies.no_signal_format_only: The format model scored this within 3 points of an empty text (66 % fake · 34 % real), so the score says nothing about these words.
bodies.unrecognised: Most of this text isn't in the English news vocabulary the models learned, so there is little for them to read.
bodies.url_only: The detector reads text only. Paste the article itself, not its address.
bodies.disagreement: The format model reacts to agency datelines and wire-service phrasing; the content model has those removed first. A split means the styling and the wording point different ways.

rows.format_note: Random forest over word patterns, including datelines and agency names.
rows.content_note: Logistic regression; agency names and datelines are removed first.
rows.format_only: Format model only — content model not loaded
rows.content_missing: not scored — model file not loaded
